English: Hand-Dug Pit
A shallow, manually dug pit lined with hides, providing the most basic water collection for a nomad clan.
Leather Water Bag Stand
A stand of stretched leather water bags, collecting rain and dew for greater storage and easier transport.
Wooden Trough
A simple but effective wooden trough, channeling and storing water for both people and animals in the camp.
Shallow Well
A hand-dug shallow well, lined with timber and stone, providing steadier access to clean water.
Animal Watering Hole
A broad, reinforced watering hole designed for large herds and riders, sustaining both people and livestock through harsh seasons.
Timbered Well
A deep, timber-reinforced well with improved lifting mechanisms, ensuring abundant fresh water for a flourishing nomad camp.
Draw Bucket Station
A robust station with pulley-driven buckets, greatly speeding water retrieval and supporting large-scale nomadic life.
Filtered Spring
A spring surrounded by stonework and reed filters, providing exceptionally clean water for both people and horses.
Covered Steppe Well
A masterwork well with timbered supports and a heavy covering, protected against sand and debris, sustaining the greatest nomad hordes.
Oasis Pavilion
A grand tented oasis, complete with shaded pools, ample storage, and gathering space for the entire clan—an unparalleled source of life in the steppe.
